To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed controller is capable of managing the hovering-to-forward flight transition and the forward-to-hovering transition for a tiltrotor UAV, while the presence of redundancy of the control actuation system is managed by the control allocation module.

a genetic algorithm based approach can be successfully employed to tune the gains of a non-linear controller designed for a tilt-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle, with the aim of managing the transition between hovering and forward flight, and of managing redundancy in the control actuation system.

the use of a genetic algorithm based optimization technique allows for a preliminary design of a fixed structure controller for a tilt-rotor unmanned air vehicle that exhibits satisfactory responses during the transition phases and that the proposed control system is able to manage the redundancy in the control actuation system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a Flight Control System for the E-Peteron UAV.
the development of a control system for the E-Peteron tilt-rotor aircraft, a small scale UAV designed and developed at Politecnico di Milano, Italy.
the development and implementation of a control logic for the management of a tilt-rotor aircraft.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a non-linear fixed-structure controller for the transition phase has been devised, its gain tuning has been performed through genetic algorithms and its effectiveness demonstrated by numerical simulations.
the results obtained are promising, and the proposed approach is a viable alternative to the design of Flight Control System architectures for tilt-rotors.
this work represents a significant contribution towards a better understanding of the design of Flight Control System for tilt-rotors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed controller is able to perform the transition from hovering to forward flight conditions and vice versa, and it is robust to the loss of control effectors.
the proposed control system is able to provide satisfactory responses in terms of stability, performance, and robustness to parameter variations.

we have been able to design a controller for the hovering and the transition phase to forward flight for the E-Peteron tiltrotor aircraft, which is a challenging task for the presence of the redundancy of the control actuators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach is suitable for the design of the Flight Control System of tilt-rotor aircraft, especially in the preliminary design phase.
the proposed approach is suitable to be implemented for a tilt-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle, and it could be extended to other classes of aircraft.
the proposed control system is able to perform the transition from hovering to forward flight, and vice-versa, with a good level of performance.
